clue.text: Maybe an earthed bulb was used to light mine

definitions.text: Maybe an earthed bulb was used to light mine

parts.words: Maybe an earthed bulb was used to light mine
parts.note: an earthed bulb sounds like an electrical precaution, but the clue means a protected flame lamp carried by miners so as not to ignite firedamp

explanation.surface: An electrician explains how a grounded light bulb lit up a pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earthed' suggests electrical wiring; read it as 'underground', and 'mine' as a coal pit, to see the miner's protected lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The Davy lamp was the classic protected light carried below ground by colliers, designed not to ignite gas.

clue.text: Thus footballers rest

parts.note: thus means so, as in 'and so it was'
the FA is the Football Association, governing body of English football

explanation.surface: So this is where the football players take a breather.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch is a piece of furniture for resting on, so the noun stands for a place of rest.

clue.text: Let go without payment

definitions.meaning: to release a captive is to set him at liberty

explanation.definitionFit: To liberate is to let go, and something gratis costs nothing; the same word covers both.

clue.text: Vegetable from jar buried in rubbish dump

indicators.note: something buried lies inside, so the jar's word sits within the dump's word

parts.note: a tip is the British word for a rubbish dump
an urn is a large jar or vase

explanation.surface: Someone digs a vegetable out of a jar dumped in a landfill site.
explanation.walkthrough: TIP is everyday British for a council rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: A root crop of the cabbage family, a common edible vegetable.

clue.text: A kookaburra apparently amused the stupid fool

parts.note: someone amused is laughing
a jackass is a stupid person, a fool

explanation.surface: An Australian bird seems to find the idiot very funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' hints that the bird's name sounds like a description of a giggling idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Australian folk name for the kookaburra, from its loud cackling call.

clue.text: Herb is even more stupid

definitions.meaning: a plant whose root gives a red dye
comparative of mad, crazier or sillier

explanation.definitionFit: Rubia tinctorum is a dye plant, and the comparative of mad means crazier.

clue.text: Sale organised for local products

indicators.note: organised suggests putting things in a new order, so the letters of sale are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sale has been arranged for produce made in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is crossword shorthand for the pub, so local products are beers.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers are what a pub (the British 'local') serves and is known for.

clue.text: Survey enough to turn one's head

definitions.meaning: to survey is to scan the surroundings
to turn the head is to glance about

explanation.walkthrough: 'enough to' is surface padding; turning one's head is the physical act of glancing about.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan the scene is to glance about, and turning the head to see behind does the same.

clue.text: Suspect retirement pay will lead to temporary lay-off

parts.note: sus is informal British for suspect or suspicion
a pension is money paid in retirement

explanation.surface: Doubts about someone's retirement income lead to their being stood down for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: SUS is British slang for suspect, as in the old 'sus laws'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension is a period when someone is barred from work or play for a time.

clue.text: Shouts for buckshee boxing contests

parts.note: buckshee is British slang for free of charge
rounds are the stages of a boxing bout

explanation.surface: Cries go up for boxing bouts with no admission fee.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'shout' is British and Australian slang for one's turn to buy drinks for the group; 'buckshee' is army slang for gratis.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts are drinks bought for a group, and gratis drinks are exactly that.

clue.text: Studies the arguments in favour

annotationWithheld.why: Studies the arguments in favour: 'Studies' gives the verb, but cons are arguments against, not in favour, so the second half does not define the answer as held.

clue.text: English writer who added weight to Deva

parts.note: Deva was the Roman name for the city of Chester
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A novelist is said to have made a Roman town heavier.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester, in Cheshire, was the Roman fort Deva.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was the English author of the Father Brown stories.

clue.text: A passage of arms for a linking of arms

definitions.meaning: a fight or battle between forces
a betrothal, a promise to marry

explanation.definitionFit: A battle between armies and a betrothal of a couple are both called by this word.

clue.text: Not so heavy as a box of matches? It's probably heavier

definitions.meaning: a pocket fire-maker, a substitute for a box of matches, is probably heavier than the box

explanation.walkthrough: 'as a box of matches?' links the two: the second sense is the gadget used instead of matches, which outweighs them.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comparative of light; the other is the gas or petrol device for igniting cigarettes.

clue.text: A match for the devil himself

definitions.meaning: an old friction match was given this brand name
the name of Satan before his fall

explanation.definitionFit: Early friction matches were sold under this name, which is also Satan's.

clue.text: Hair-waving accessories producing great waves

definitions.meaning: curlers used to set hair in waves
long heavy swells breaking on a shore

explanation.definitionFit: Curlers set hair, and big breakers rolling in from the sea share the name.

clue.text: Put an end to that chat-line ob session

definitions.text: Put an end to that chat-line
definitions.meaning: to end a phone call by replacing the receiver
an obsession or fixation, split oddly in print

explanation.definitionFit: Ending a telephone call and a neurotic fixation share this phrase.

clue.text: To reverse in speed, turn around

indicators.note: in places the reversed little word inside the word for speed

parts.note: rate means speed, as in 'at a rate of knots'

indicators.note: reverse says the word to is read backwards

explanation.surface: Instructions for backing up quickly and then spinning round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To reverse in speed' reads like a driving instruction; the comma splits off the definition, 'turn around'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spin or revolve is to go round on an axis.

clue.text: They moved along ship lanes to the South

indicators.note: moved signals that the letters of along ship lanes are shifted into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Vessels sailed down the shipping routes towards the southern seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges ALONG SHIP LANES; S for 'the South' is added; 'They' is the definition, the whole clue describing the treasure ships.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun points to the treasure ships of Spain, which sailed the sea lanes to the Americas.

clue.text: The Spanish even supply a cricket team

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: The Spanish even provide a cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket team has this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side fields a number of players equal to this count, hence the team's name.

clue.text: North American tree blazed by jungle patrols

parts.note: a palm is a tropical tree

explanation.surface: A tree from northern America is set alight by soldiers in the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'something blazed by jungle patrols', a nod to the jellied incendiary used in Vietnam.
explanation.definitionFit: This jellied petrol was the incendiary weapon fired in jungle warfare, notably in Vietnam.

clue.text: Proton smashed very rapidly

indicators.note: smashed suggests breaking apart, so the letters of proton are reassembled

explanation.surface: A particle is split in an accelerator at great speed.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word means at once, quickly.

clue.text: A steep adjustment to Iberian money

indicators.note: adjustment suggests rearranging, so the letters of a steep are reordered

explanation.surface: A sharp revaluation of the Spanish currency.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the unit of currency in Spain before the euro.

clue.text: Stock properties

parts.note: reads like shares on the market, but means farm holdings where livestock is kept

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' suggests stocks and shares; here it is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Large farms raising cattle or sheep are holdings defined by their livestock.

clue.text: Second person indicates which letter is most common in English

definitions.meaning: the archaic second-person pronoun, object form of thou

definitions.text: which letter is most common in English
definitions.meaning: the letter E is the most frequent in English, so the phrase names that letter with the definite article

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: 'which letter is most common' is answered by naming that letter with 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic object form of thou is the old second-person pronoun.

clue.text: Desert in which I bog up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read from bottom to top, so I bog runs backwards

explanation.surface: A traveller gets stuck in a marsh in the wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses I BOG, giving the four-letter run.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the great desert of Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: How to express a plurality of purposes

definitions.text: How to express a plurality of purposes

parts.words: How to express a plurality of purposes
parts.note: asks for the plural form of a word meaning purpose or function

explanation.definitionFit: Several purposes or functions are expressed by the plural of the word for a purpose.

clue.text: Gaunt American lawyer in cave has a sour disposition

indicators.note: in places the lawyer inside the hollow

parts.note: taken as written
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters of sour are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A thin US attorney sulks in a cavern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament, matching 'sour', but signals rearrangement; 'has a' only links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpse-like means pale and emaciated, hollow-cheeked.

clue.text: Whereat talent-spotters angle for promising cricketers

definitions.text: Whereat talent-spotters angle for promising cricketers

parts.words: Whereat talent-spotters angle for promising cricketers
parts.note: angle suggests fishing gear, but the place is the practice enclosure where young batsmen are scouted

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket practice takes place in netted enclosures; scouts 'angle' there as if fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Netted practice areas are where coaches watch young cricketers, and fishermen use mesh too.

clue.text: Diplomats from the East don't catch the night Constellation

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
to miss is to fail to catch
Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Envoys from the Orient fail to spot the stars at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Envoys sent on missions represent a government abroad.
